Summary: The change extends ValueTracking’s non-equality reasoning to look through PHI-based simple recurrences when both operands are recurrence PHIs in the same loop and their recurrence steps are related by an invertible operator. top_candidates.subject: Look through invertible recurrences in isKnownNonEqual
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The change extends ValueTracking’s non-equality reasoning to look through PHI-based simple recurrences when both operands are recurrence PHIs in the same loop and their recurrence steps are related by an invertible operator. It adds a new PHI case in getInvertibleOperand that matches simple recurrences, recurses on the recurrence-forming operators to identify an invertible operand position, and then maps the PHI operands back to the start-vs-step relationship. The accompanying analysis test updates expected results so several recurrence-vs-recurrence comparisons now fold directly to false instead of producing an icmp equality expression.
Mechanisms: ValueTracking invertible-operand analysis extended to PHI recurrences; Simple recurrence matching via matchSimpleRecurrence; Recursive comparison of recurrence-step operators through getInvertibleOperand; Loop/PHI reasoning for proving two evolving values remain equal or non-equal; Constant-folding / known-non-equal propagation for arithmetic recurrences
Touched symbols: getInvertibleOperand; matchSimpleRecurrence; PHINode; BinaryOperator; llvm::ValueTracking; known-non-equal.ll
Risk relevance: Touches core analysis code used by optimizer queries about equality/non-equality, so mistakes can affect InstCombine and downstream simplification decisions; Adds new recursive reasoning in getInvertibleOperand, increasing the chance of assertion failures or incorrect operand-index assumptions when PHI recurrences are nested or malformed; Uses strict assertions about operand identity and PHI structure, which can surface latent miscompilations or crashes on unusual IR patterns; The change alters semantics of known-non-equal inference, a high-risk area for optimizer regressions because it can change whether comparisons fold to constants
Build risk: Adds new test expectations in llvm/test/Analysis/ValueTracking/known-non-equal.ll, so test coverage shifts with optimizer behavior; No build-system changes, but analysis-only logic can affect many optimization tests indirectly through shared ValueTracking queries; The new code path is guarded by structural matching and recursion, which may be sensitive to IR shape variations in future tests

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This change updates several libc++ unordered-container debug-mode tests so they construct non-empty containers explicitly before taking iterators. The tests now insert or initialize elements, compute the relevant bucket for local iterators, and add assertions that the obtained iterator is not equal to the bucket/end iterator before advancing or comparing against end. The substantive intent is to make the iterator-debug checks operate on valid populated containers rather than on default-constructed empty ones.
Mechanisms: Test coverage adjustment for unordered container iterator debug mode; Local-iterator/bucket selection logic exercised via bucket(key) and begin(bucket); Iterator validity assertions against end()/end(bucket) after container population; Construction path differences between default construction plus insert and initializer-list construction
